nodes.claim: At prior .5 and fixed +6/−4 payoffs with price1, two binary signal models A=(sensitivity.6,specificity1) and B=(1,.6) have accuracy.8 but strictly different optimal purchase actions.
nodes.certificate: Declared input, checked in the cited fixture.

nodes.claim: A summary-only deterministic selector receives identical input in A andB.
nodes.certificate: Declared summary contains prior, payoffs, price and overall accuracy, all equal.

nodes.claim: Act-now is optimal among buy/now in A, and buy is optimal in B.
nodes.certificate: FRQ42 exact net values are A:.8 versus1 and B:1.2 versus1.

nodes.claim: The conditional observation distributions differ even though overall accuracy matches.
nodes.certificate: The root gives different sensitivity/specificity pairs.

nodes.claim: A deterministic function of that identical summary returns the same choice in both models.
nodes.certificate: Equal inputs to a deterministic function have equal outputs.

nodes.claim: Repeating the unchanged summary supplies no distinction between A andB.
nodes.certificate: Each repetition contains the same values.

nodes.claim: The identical accuracy label alone does not identify the confusion matrix.
nodes.certificate: A andB are distinct matrices consistent with that label and prior.

nodes.claim: That same buy/now output is suboptimal in at least one of A orB.
nodes.certificate: R3 establishes opposite strict optima; one common choice cannot equal both.

nodes.claim: A fixed always-buy selector loses .2 relative to the optimum in A.
nodes.certificate: A buy=.8 while now=1.

nodes.claim: A fixed always-now selector loses .2 relative to the optimum in B.
nodes.certificate: B now=1 while buy=1.2.

nodes.claim: No deterministic selector restricted to that summary is optimal in both admitted models.
nodes.certificate: Any such selector has a common output, and the parent covers both possible actions.

nodes.claim: Choosing a more confident label for the same output does not remove its .2 payoff deficit in the losing case.
nodes.certificate: Confidence label is not part of the fixed payoff calculation.

nodes.claim: A claim of uniform optimality must therefore change an admitted condition or acquire a distinguishing input.
nodes.certificate: With model set, summary and criterion fixed, the parent contradiction remains.

nodes.claim: Adding a new feature that is constant across A andB leaves the selector inputs identical.
nodes.certificate: Concatenating equal summary with an equal constant preserves equality.

nodes.claim: An observed feature that identifies A versusB would remove this particular ambiguity.
nodes.certificate: The selector could choose the model’s known strict optimum from R3.

nodes.claim: Relaxing uniform optimality to a regret objective changes the guarantee being requested.
nodes.certificate: The criterion no longer requires zero loss in each model.

nodes.claim: A deterministic selector using the summary plus that constant feature still returns the same action in both models.
nodes.certificate: The parent preserves identical full input; deterministic equality applies again.

nodes.claim: An additional description of “80% reliable” derived only from accuracy is one such constant feature.
nodes.certificate: It is a fixed function of the equal accuracy value.

nodes.claim: More decimal places on the unchanged .8 value are also nondiscriminating here.
nodes.certificate: Exact root accuracy is equal, not merely rounded equality.

nodes.claim: The constant-feature augmentation still leaves at least one strict .2 loss among the admitted models.
nodes.certificate: Its common action is either buy or now; R9/R10 give the corresponding losing model.

nodes.claim: The augmentation cannot truthfully certify zero regret for both models.
nodes.certificate: The parent provides a nonzero-loss case.

nodes.claim: A narrower model set containing only A or only B removes the two-model contradiction but adds a model-identification premise.
nodes.certificate: A single retained model has one specified optimum; exclusion of the other is additional information.

nodes.claim: A’s positive-signal gross contribution is1.8 and its negative contribution if acting is−.8.
nodes.certificate: Direct products .5×.6×6 and .5×.4×6−.5×1×4.

nodes.claim: B’s positive contribution is2.2 and its negative contribution is−1.2.
nodes.certificate: Direct products .5×1×6−.5×.4×4 and0−.5×.6×4.

nodes.claim: Declining after negative signals is optimal for both models under the declared linear payoff.
nodes.certificate: The negative contribution is below0 and declining yields0 there.

nodes.claim: At prior .5, both accuracies equal half the sum of sensitivity and specificity, namely.8.
nodes.certificate: Each pair sums to1.6.

nodes.claim: The shared accuracy constraint permits more than the two displayed matrices.
nodes.certificate: Sensitivity a in[.6,1] and false-positive rate a−.6 preserve.8.

nodes.claim: The two displayed matrices therefore establish non-identification without proving they exhaust the source’s possibilities.
nodes.certificate: Two witnesses suffice for nonuniqueness; no exhaustive-source premise is given.

nodes.claim: An exact repeated display is not an independent observation of the hidden state or model.
nodes.certificate: The repeated values are copied from the same summary by premise.

nodes.claim: If a later display contains a new conditional rate, it is outside the unchanged-summary branch.
nodes.certificate: The data now differ in a decision-relevant coordinate.

nodes.claim: Future access to such a rate remains a separate empirical/channel question.
nodes.certificate: The formal model supplies no future retrieval event.

nodes.claim: Different conditional matrices can be compatible with the same aggregate check.
nodes.certificate: A andB supply exact witnesses.

nodes.claim: Verifying only aggregate accuracy cannot select between these two matrices.
nodes.certificate: Both pass exactly the same aggregate equality.

nodes.claim: A test of sensitivity or specificity can distinguish A fromB if one of these two is known to be the actual model.
nodes.certificate: The two given conditional rates differ; the two-model restriction is explicit.

nodes.claim: Changing price to0 makes buy’s net value1.8 in A.
nodes.certificate: Remove the price1 subtraction from gross1.8.

nodes.claim: This zero-price comparison extends the original paid case rather than refuting it.
nodes.certificate: The price premise has changed while both arithmetic results stand.

nodes.claim: The regret .2 is measured in the declared payoff units, not as an error probability.
nodes.certificate: It is1−.8, a utility difference.

nodes.claim: A mixed policy buying with probability q has regret .2(1−q) in B.
nodes.certificate: Expected mixture payoff q×1.2+(1−q)×1; subtract from optimum1.2.

nodes.claim: The same mixture has regret .2q in A.
nodes.certificate: Expected mixture payoff q×.8+(1−q)×1; subtract from optimum1.

nodes.claim: A stochastic policy is outside the deterministic-selector impossibility statement.
nodes.certificate: Its distribution may be fixed while the realized choice varies; expected regret is a new criterion.

nodes.claim: A valid distinguishing feature need not be the entire confusion matrix.
nodes.certificate: Within the explicitly exhaustive A/B fixture, a single model-identity bit suffices.

nodes.claim: An arbitrary feature name without different values is insufficient.
nodes.certificate: The deep branch R14–R20 shows equality remains.

nodes.claim: Abstaining from the uniform-optimality claim preserves the model ambiguity without inventing a missing rate.
nodes.certificate: It changes the claim made, not the given observations.

nodes.claim: For the exhaustive two-model set, worst expected regret of the q mixture is max(.2q,.2(1−q)).
nodes.certificate: The two side expansions enumerate all model regrets under that added scope.

nodes.claim: This maximum is minimized at q=.5 with value.1.
nodes.certificate: The increasing and decreasing linear terms intersect at.1; moving either direction raises their maximum.

nodes.claim: The .1 minimax regret does not supply zero regret or identify the true model.
nodes.certificate: Both models retain positive expected regret at q=.5 and no new likelihood is observed.
